mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% per month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis period when risk premia spike independently.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when supply shocks (INDPRO falls) offset demand weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of offsetting fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, reducing corporate sales and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when offset by strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflationary environment, where higher rates and prices erode real cash flows and investor sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth offsetting cost pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 15% signals a collapse in residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and drags on equities via lower capital expenditures, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of offsetting fiscal stimulus to housing.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (unemployment) signals a paradoxical labor market where employment expands but underemployment rises, indicating weak wage growth and consumer confidence, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market slack with job quality deterioration
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity gains.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average signals that households are depleting savings buffers, which reduces their capacity to sustain consumption, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong fiscal stimulus.
